title.narrative: Drought/fires emergency response - Yanomami Indigenous Territory

description.narrative:
Droughts and forest fires which began in early February in the state of Roraima, North Brazil, have recently intensified, resulting in serious impacts on 2,030 indigenous people (935 women and 1,095 men) living in 19 remote communities in the Amazon rainforest, in Yanomami indigenous territory. These have been caused by the changing frequency and intensity of phenomena such as El Niño, making this the worst registered drought in 20 years in the state of Roraima – 13 of 15 municipalities have been declared in a state of emergency by the State Governor, Suely Campos. Small streams, tributaries and Amazonian wells close to the communities have dried up, and crops and houses have been burnt forcing communities to relocate to other areas. Main impacts on Yanomami indigenous people are: lack of drinking water and water for crops, lack of access to food, health issues such as smoke-induced respiratory problems, especially in young children, and displacement of communities.
This project aims to secure access to food security and clean drinking water for 7 of the most affected communities - 1,170 people (512 women, 372 children aged 0-9, and 286 men) - by the fires and droughts. These communities are: Hatyanai (Apiaú region); Piau, Rasasi, Maraxi Bora and Apiahik (Totootopi region); and Homoxi e Koriaupë (Surucucu region) - in Yanomami Indigenous Territory. Main activities include: purchase and installation of 80 water filters in 4 communities; training of 8 Indigenous Environmental and Sanitation Agents and and booklet produced in Yanomami language on filter set-up and maintenance in 4 communities; purchase and distribution of 95 agricultural tools to 3 communities; distribution of 365 food baskets to 3 communities; and planting of fruit seedlings in 1 community after the rainy season near homes to benefit women and children.
